descriptionChirho: A physical house or dwelling place, the primary concrete sense of oikos. Used extensively for domestic residences (Matt 9:6-7; Mark 2:1, 11, 26; 3:20; 5:19, 38; 7:17, 30; Luke 16:4; Acts 8:3; 20:20), the Jerusalem temple as God's house (Matt 21:13; Mark 11:17), and houses in the plural (Matt 11:8; 1 Tim 3:12; Titus 1:11). All multilingual glosses converge: Arabic bayt/buyut, German Haus, French maison, Hebrew bayit/batim, Hindi ghar, Korean jip, Spanish casa.

The household or family as a social unit, extending beyond the physical building to mean the people who inhabit it. Used of managing one's household (1 Tim 3:12) and of households being overturned by false teaching (Titus 1:11). The English glosses shift from 'house' to 'household', and the Arabic buyutahum and Hindi gharon similarly indicate the people/family rather than the structure.
